terra.problem: Saying the first-day schedule keeps the week's spending from using up the money and prevents scrambling adds reasons the text does not give.
Saying that starting on the first day means there will be something to set aside adds a guarantee the text does not give.
The text says the Corinthians recommend the carriers, but does not say they are choosing people they know to be trustworthy.
The text does not mention armor or swords, but saying there are none adds details it leaves open.
The text does not say the carriers will walk to Jerusalem.
The delivery-address joke repeats the joke idea used in the preceding explanation.
The passage does not say Timothy carries the gift, but it also does not say he carries nothing.
The snack comparison mentions food other than cookies.
Saying Apollos was not ready adds a reason for his not going. Paul says he was not inclined to go now.
Paul says Apollos will go when he has the opportunity; the text does not state Apollos's own plans.
Converts are not necessarily the first people in a place to believe. Paul says Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia.
Saying the men lifted spirits instead of testing them adds a contrast the text does not make.
